name: SC-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about 21 points Republican and incumbent Sheri Biggs was renominated
Biggs holds a roughly seven-to-one fundraising advantage over Eunice Lehmacher ($692k to $93k)
No public general-election polling and no expert raters flag the race as competitive
Prediction markets price Biggs at roughly 96 percent
model.rationale: The district's 21-point Republican lean, Biggs' renomination, and her overwhelming fundraising edge leave no credible path for Lehmacher, and prediction markets reflect that at about 96 percent Republican. Even with a national environment that could favor Democrats, the structural deficit here is far too large to close.
model.watch: A significant scandal involving Biggs or unexpected outside spending against her would be the main development capable of narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 3rd District is deeply Republican, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. Representative Sheri Biggs secured renomination and enters the general election as a heavy favorite over Democrat Eunice Lehmacher, with Libertarian Brian Corriea also on the ballot. No public general-election polling exists for this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

The financial picture strongly favors the incumbent: Biggs has raised roughly $692,000 and holds about $259,000 on hand, while Lehmacher has raised about $93,000. Prediction markets price Biggs' chances at roughly 96 percent. Even accounting for a national environment that may tilt toward Democrats in 2026, the district's fundamentals make an upset very unlikely, and Biggs is expected to win comfortably.
